text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Tension seems to have eased in the Herzegovinian town of Mostar following several days of skirmishes between the local Moslem and Croat populations.
- Croatia and the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation agree on ways of further cooperation.
- Two smaller opposition parties to form a new centrist democratic association.
- An estimated 94.29 billion kuna needed to build and repair road network in the country.
- Unemployment rises in the eastern town of Osijek. Total jobless up 13.4 percent from the end of August 1995.
- Damage caused by recent quakes in the Dubrovnik area estimated at 100 million kuna.
- Government decides to raise pensions by 5.6 percent as of Sept 1. Pensioners' Union threatens with a strike later this month unless a 40-percent rise is approved.
- Head of the Hague war crimes tribunal says more indictments will be issued for crimes committed in Vukovar. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
